To determine how much salt Jack will get when all the water evaporates, we need to follow these steps:

1. Calculate the amount of salt in the original 2 liters of seawater.
2. Convert the amount of salt from liters to milliliters (ml).

First, we calculate the amount of salt in the original 2 liters of seawater. Since the seawater is 20% salt, we can find the amount of salt by multiplying the total volume of the seawater by the percentage of salt:

\[ \text{Amount of salt} = 2 \, \text{liters} \times 0.20 = 0.4 \, \text{liters} \]

Next, we convert the amount of salt from liters to milliliters. Since 1 liter is equal to 1000 milliliters, we multiply the amount of salt in liters by 1000:

\[ \text{Amount of salt in milliliters} = 0.4 \, \text{liters} \times 1000 \, \text{ml/liter} = 400 \, \text{ml} \]

So, the amount of salt Jack will get when all the water evaporates is \(\boxed{400}\) ml.
